mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate a slowdown in consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a decline in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between RSAFS decrease and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies benefit from increased production and efficiency.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of HOUST increase and UNRATE decrease on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 month-over-month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained growth in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals a strong economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters when GDPC1 grows by more than 2%, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
